#### Session analytics — stack and heap at every step

**What is being answered.** What choosing session windows actually requires of the analytics store, as a store you can watch fill.

`keyOf(s)` is the detail everything turns on: the row key is **("key", session start)**, so when a merge moves the start, the session needs a *different row*. A fixed window's correction is an update; this is an erase plus a write.

`run(key, gap, canErase)` is the pipeline, and the `canErase` flag is the store's capability. With it, one row holding 11; without it, two rows totalling 18 for a session worth 11 — and no error anywhere.

The animation steps through the code, holding each line long enough to read the STACK (call frames and their locals) and the HEAP (allocated arrays and objects) as they are AT THAT MOMENT. Expand any step to study it on its own.

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch04-system-memory/ch04-system-memory.svg" alt="Session analytics — stack and heap at every step, 4 steps showing stack and heap" width="980">

<details>
<summary><b>Step 1 of 4</b> — the row key is the session's BOUNDS, which is the whole problem</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch04-system-memory/frames/step-01.svg" alt="Step 1: the row key is the session&#39;s BOUNDS, which is the whole problem" width="980">

`keyOf(s)` is ("b", 90) — the key includes the session's START. So when the start later moves to 50, the same session needs a DIFFERENT row. That is the structural difference from a fixed window, whose bounds never move.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 2 of 4</b> — so a correction is an ERASE plus a write</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch04-system-memory/frames/step-02.svg" alt="Step 2: so a correction is an ERASE plus a write" width="980">

At index 7, `now.start` (50) differs from `old.start` (90), so the old row is erased and the new one written. The store ends with ONE row holding 11. Two store operations for one logical correction.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 3 of 4</b> — without the erase, the old row survives</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch04-system-memory/frames/step-03.svg" alt="Step 3: without the erase, the old row survives" width="980">

With `canErase` false the `erase` is skipped and the write still happens, so `broken` holds TWO rows: 7 and 11, totalling 18 for one session worth 11. Nothing errored. The store just has a row for a session that never existed.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 4 of 4</b> — and the state size is decided by the data, not the schema</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch04-system-memory/frames/step-04.svg" alt="Step 4: and the state size is decided by the data, not the schema" width="980">

`entries` = 5 for 9 events at gap 120, and 6 at gap 40. There is no expression here that depends only on the schema — the count comes from how bursty the data was. A fixed-window pipeline's state is (keys × open windows) and can be sized in advance; this cannot.

</details>
